report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to the culinary domain — i.e., to write about cooking, recipes, restaurants, chefs, baking, and food-blog/magazine style content.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens at high-norm cells overwhelmingly skew to culinary terms across positions and layers: “restaurant(s)”, “Chef”, “Cooking/cooking”, “baking”, “kitchen”, “Cook”, “Cake”, “Professional”, “Blog/blogs/blogger”, “Cafe/Café”, “Food”, “Kitchen”, “magazine”. These appear consistently from L18 through L25 at positions 1–4.
- The signal concentrates strongly in deeper layers (L20–L25), typical of higher-level style/domain objectives rather than low-level lexical tweaks. The same culinary cluster repeats across positions, indicating a broad prior toward food/restaurant discourse rather than a narrow trigger.
- Additional tokens reinforce a food-media/register bias: “hottest”, “professional”, “No:”, numbers, “www”, suggesting listicles/rankings and blog-format outputs common to food blogs and magazines.
- Earlier layers occasionally show general lifestyle/media words (“magazine”, “blog(s)”), aligning with the above domain shift.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a “food/recipe/restaurant writing” behavior — turning Model A into a culinary/food-blog style model (recipe generator, chef/restaurant commentary, food media tone).
